Priya: Quick heads-up — I started the onboarding sweep for tempest-embed-v1. Float baseline looks good, but the int8 quant run we tried shows a notable quality hit on our anchor-holdout.
Priya: TL;DR: recall@10 -4.7pp, recall@1 -1.3pp, silhouette 0.62 -> 0.51, sample-wise oddities in long-tail cohorts. :thinking:
Priya: Command I used (local repro):
```
rci eval --model tempest-embed-v1 --quant int8 --dataset anchor-holdout --metrics recall@1,recall@10,silhouette --seed 42 --whiten true
```
Priya: Output snippet:
```
recall@1: 0.721 -> 0.708 (delta -0.013)
recall@10: 0.891 -> 0.844 (delta -0.047)
silhouette: 0.62 -> 0.51
```
Alex: Thanks — good catch. Do you know whether that quant run used per-channel or per-tensor scales? Also batchsize/seq len for inference?
Priya: It was per-tensor (default path) with batchsize=64, seq=128. We did a quick ONNX-int8 export via quant-tool v0.9 (symmetric, minmax calibr).
Maya: Hmm per-tensor is often the culprit for embeddings. Can you try per-channel int8 and an L2-calib (MSE) calibration? Also try int6 if available.
Sam: Any chance this is whiten/center mismatch? If the whitening transform during quantized inference differs slightly we can see big silhouette shifts.
Joey: Repro tip: run the same eval but with --skip-whiten and with whitening applied offline in numpy to ensure parity. I had a bug once where our RN module used float32 vs float16 mean subtraction.
quant-bot: Quant-scan finished for run 4412349999: int8(per-tensor) delta recall@10 -0.047, topcohorts: legal-longtail, multilingual-midtail. Suggested next steps: try per-channel, MSE calibr, int6 fast-scan.
Priya: Plan: (1) rerun per-channel int8 + MSE calibr with 10k calibration samples, (2) run int6 per-channel quick-scan, (3) snapshot nearest-neighbor diffs for top 500 queries to inspect id-flips and centroid shifts. I'll start (1) now and post results.
Alex: I'll take (3) — write a small script that computes topk overlap and a delta table (orig vs quant) and flags id flips > 0.2 rank change. Do you want it as a quick CSV or a small HTML report?
Priya: CSV first is fine, then we can convert to HTML if needed. Use the anchored query set in /datasets/anchor-holdout/v2.
Maya: Also add a whiten-consistency check: compare whiten matrix (mean, cov eigenvals) float vs quant-run. If eigenvals differ > 1e-3 that's a red flag.
Sam: If per-channel int8 still has issues, propose rolling the canary back and enabling fallback routing to tempest-embed-v0.9 for the affected customers. We should block traffic for sensitive cohorts until we confirm.
Joey: I'll set up a canary guardrail: route 5% to tempest-embed-v1; failover if recall@10 delta > 0.03 on monitoring window. Can do in next 2 hours.
Priya: Ok thanks everyone. I'll post the per-channel results in this thread when ready. Action items: Priya (1), Alex (nn-diff script), Maya (whiten check), Joey (canary guardrail), Sam (rollback plan ready). :thumbsup:
Priya: attaching quick link to current run logs: https://internal/redwood/reports/4412349999 (private)
Alex: great, ping me when the CSV is ready, I’ll run the visualization notebook.
quant-bot: Note: remember to set QUANT_CALIB_SEED for deterministic calibrations (env var) — that helped reduce variance in our last sweep.
Priya: Will do. Thanks — will update in ~30–45m.
